review_notes: Read the whole file and focused on repeated reasoning. The `cont` discrete-topology blocks in swapCoind/diagonalCoind/insertCoind are short boilerplate, so I did not report them. The hfirst/hthird pairs inside insert_homotopy_raw repeat a short congrArg-plus-simp step, and I did not report that either. The one substantial duplication is the Fin.sum_univ_succ / removeNth-cons splitting of the alternating sum, which appears in resolutionEval_d (succ case) and in hthird' of insert_homotopy_raw. I grepped the formal-frontier repo and Mathlib's ContCohomology directory and found no existing lemma for this split. The replacement is untested because I cannot run Lean. In particular, the `φ` unification and the exact form of the simp normal forms may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: Splitting the alternating sum over `Fin (n+2)` at index 0 is done by hand here, using `Fin.sum_univ_succ`, `Fin.removeNth_zero`, `Fin.tail_cons`, `removeNth_succ_cons`, `Fin.val_succ`, `pow_succ` and `simp; abel`. The same reasoning is redone in `insert_homotopy_raw` (`hthird'`, lines 342-352). There it uses the same `rw [.., Fin.sum_univ_succ]`, `simp only [Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons, TopRep.removeNth_succ_cons, Fin.val_succ, pow_succ]` and `simp; abel`. The cons-splitting fact is never stated, so it is rediscovered with a fragile simp set in each proof. The private helper `removeNth_succ_cons` is also exposed only to be re-invoked in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma next to `removeNth_succ_cons` (placed before `resolutionEval_d`), with `{A : Type*} [AddCommGroup A]`:

`private theorem alternatingSum_removeNth_cons {A} [AddCommGroup A] (n : ℕ) (φ : (Fin (n+1) → G) → A) (t : G) (hs : Fin (n+1) → G) : ∑ j : Fin (n+2), (-1 : ℤ)^j.val • φ (j.removeNth (Fin.cons t hs : Fin (n+2) → G)) = φ hs - ∑ j : Fin (n+1), (-1 : ℤ)^j.val • φ (Fin.cons t (j.removeNth hs))`.

Proof sketch: `rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]`; then `simp only [Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons, removeNth_succ_cons, Fin.val_succ, pow_succ]`; then `simp; abel`. This is the existing tactic block, with the φ-specific parts abstracted away.

Use 1, the succ case of `resolutionEval_d`: after `rw [resolutionEval_sub]` and the `hs_eq` rewrite, apply the lemma with `φ := resolutionEval Y (n+1) f`, `t := hs 0` and `hs := Fin.tail hs`. Then rewrite `resolutionEval_succ` and `Fin.cons_zero` to turn `φ (cons (hs 0) (j.removeNth (tail hs)))` into `resolutionEval Y n (f (hs 0)) (j.removeNth (tail hs))`. Finish with the inductive hypothesis `resolutionEval_d Y n (f (hs 0)) (Fin.tail hs)`; the goal then closes by `rfl`/`sub_right_inj`.

Use 2, `hthird'` in `insert_homotopy_raw`: `rw [hthird]; exact alternatingSum_removeNth_cons (m+1) (fun s => (TopRep.resolutionEval F (m+2) f s) t) t hs`. The statement of `hthird'` is exactly this instance, up to beta, with `n = m+1` and `hs : Fin (m+2) → G`. Both uses live in the same file, so no new imports are needed, and the hypotheses are only that `A` is an additive commutative group, which `Y` and `C(G,Y)` evaluations satisfy.
findings.benefit: The alternating-sum splitting becomes a named fact with one proof. `resolutionEval_d` then reads as 'subtract the inductive instance', and `hthird'` becomes a one-line application. Later edits to the removeNth/cons API or to the sign convention need changing in one place instead of two fragile `simp` scripts. The sign bookkeeping, which is the real content, is separated from the resolution-specific rewriting.
